cards.title: Derive every cut from one pure timeline plan shared by compose and recorders
acceptance: planFilm(script with two acts, takes, {xfade: 300}) where act 1's last beat has a clip that fills its beat -> that clip's start+keep <= act 2's first placed beat start (today compose.mjs:468 trims only to the beat's own end, so the clip runs 300 ms under act 2's first clip)

cards.body:
## Summary
The film pipeline's schedule (where each beat, clip, speed-up label and caption lands) is derived three times: inline in compose.mjs take mode, again inline in film mode, and a third time as restated hold/caption rules in record-desktop.mjs and placeholders.mjs. Extract it as one pure, tested derivation, `scripts/lib/timeline.mjs`, and make every script a thin IO shell over it.

## Description
media-playback/timeline-scheduling: 'the schedule is a derivation of the timeline model, recomputed by a named function ... never hand-patched in place', and seams must not gap or overlap. Today compose.mjs (610 lines) interleaves ffprobe, filtergraph strings and the placement maths, so neither mode can be tested without ffmpeg and real takes, and the two copies have already diverged: film mode lets a clip run `xfade` ms under the next act's first clip (compose.mjs:468 vs :417), take mode warns of a trim it never does (:196). record-desktop.mjs restates src/script.ts's hold rule but not its stale-clip filter, so the desktop segment paces to a clip length the web recorder refuses. The plan module exposes planTake, planFilm, layClips (one clip-laying rule that trims a clip at the next clip's start, not just its own beat's end), holdOf/captionOf, and ffmpegArgs(plan). compose.mjs keeps its flags and output; --dry prints the plan. A parity test imports src/script.ts read-only so the .mjs and .ts hold rules cannot drift again (test-harness/pin-the-call-not-the-name: pin behaviour, not text).

## Flow
- snapshot today's `--dry` argv for the placeholder fixture (guard)
- write timeline.test.mjs cases 0-7; watch 0, 2, 3, 4 fail
- extract lib/timeline.mjs from compose.mjs; fix the seam and the take-mode overlap inside layClips
- compose.mjs: parse args -> probe durations -> plan -> ffmpegArgs -> spawn
- record-desktop.mjs and placeholders.mjs import holdOf/captionOf (record-desktop also reads the narration manifest for staleness)
- add `test:unit` to package.json; README 'Recording a take' names it

## Expected impact
A crossfaded or overlapping-beat cut can no longer lay two voices on top of each other; the desktop segment paces the same as the web segment after a script edit; the film pipeline gains its first offline tests, so the next change to compose is a reviewed diff of a plan rather than a re-render and a listen.

## Evaluation
Claim: one derivation closes the seam-overlap and hold-drift class across take, film and desktop recorder
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no module; cases 0, 2, 4 are live defects)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases under node --test, plus the argv snapshot
Result: better
Gate: none
cards.evidence: compose.mjs:468 `const room = Math.max(0, Math.min(beat.end, totalMs) - beat.start);` with compose.mjs:413-418 `p.at = at; at += p.ms - fade;` -> last beat of piece i ends at p_i.at+p_i.ms, first beat of piece i+1 starts at p_i.at+p_i.ms-fade. compose.mjs:196-198 warns and pushes the clip unchanged. record-desktop.mjs:82 comment 'src/script.ts's hold rule, restated for a plain .mjs'; :248 `JSON.parse(readFileSync(durationsPath))` with no manifest check, vs src/script.ts:146 `if (script !== undefined && isStale(id, script, narrated)) continue;`. captionOf at src/script.ts:204, record-desktop.mjs:93, placeholders.mjs:82. grep for tests of scripts/*.mjs: none; package.json test = playwright test.

cards.title: narrate re-voices exactly the beats a script edit changed, shown before it spends
acceptance: beat 1.3's line edited to a different line of the SAME length, take/audio/1.3.mp3 on disk, manifest sha from the old line -> planNarration(...).synthesize == ['1.3'] (today narrate.mjs:440 skips it because the mp3 exists, and src/script.ts isStale compares length only, so the old clip is kept silently)

beat 1.3's line edited, plain run (no --force, no --only), 1.3 not re-synthesised (e.g. its synthesis failed) -> the manifest entry for 1.3 keeps the old sha and old chars (today narrate.mjs:489 writes the NEW line's length against the OLD mp3, which hides the stale clip from src/script.ts isStale)
every beat unchanged: sha matches and mp3 on disk -> plan.reuse holds all ids and plan.spend == 0 chars

--dry with 1.3.mp3 on disk and its sha matching -> durations.json keeps the ffprobe-measured ms for 1.3; only beats with no current clip get estimates (adopts stabilize-2026-10-16 'narrate --dry overwrites the measured lengths of clips already on disk')
ELEVENLABS_VOICE_MIRA now names a different voice than the manifest records for mira -> every mira beat is in plan.synthesize with reason 'voice', narrator and athena beats are reused
legacy manifest entry with no sha whose chars equal the current line's length -> reused and marked 'legacy' in the plan, not re-spent (no surprise bill on upgrade)
--only 1.3 with 1.3 and 2.1 both changed -> plan.synthesize == ['1.3'] and plan.staleOutOfScope == ['2.1'], printed in the summary
a plan whose spend exceeds 20,000 chars without --yes -> exit 4 before any fetch call (fetch stub never invoked)

examples/journey/scripts/narrate.mjs:489 - after measuring the OLD mp3 the manifest records `chars: beat.line.length` of the NEW line
examples/journey/src/script.ts:176 - isStale compares manifest chars to line length only; the laundered entry from :489 makes it report fresh
examples/journey/scripts/narrate.mjs:376 - --dry writes an estimate for every beat in scope over measured lengths (stabilize-2026-10-16 finding, open)
examples/journey/README.md 'Re-takes' - 'A script edit is `pnpm narrate -- --only <ids> --force`': the operator must know which ids changed
examples/journey/scripts/narrate.mjs:251 - each synthesis is paid ElevenLabs characters; CHAR_BUDGET 20,000 at :42

cards.body:
## Summary
Re-taking narration after a script edit today means knowing which beat ids changed and forcing them; a plain `pnpm narrate` keeps the old clips AND rewrites the manifest so the recorder can no longer tell they are stale. Make narration content-addressed: each manifest beat carries a sha of (line, role, voice id, settings, model), and a plain run plans the diff, prints it, and voices exactly what changed.

## Description
The operator surface is the narrate CLI and the take it feeds. The decision 'which beats need new audio' is made blind although the script and the manifest hold everything needed to answer it. Worse, the default path launders: narrate.mjs:440 skips an edited beat because its mp3 exists, then :489 records the new line's length against the old clip, so src/script.ts:176 isStale (a length check) reports fresh and the take holds the picture for the old clip's length under the new line. deterministic-prefix-caching/hash-inputs-and-pipeline: 'the name must change when the entry's content would' - key the clip on everything that decides its audio, and give the operator one command. The plan module (pure, injected fs/cast) returns {synthesize[{id, reason: line|voice|settings|model|new|missing}], reuse, legacy, staleOutOfScope, spend}; narrate prints it as a table before any spend, `--plan` stops there, `--dry` estimates only beats with no current clip, and the manifest keeps writing `chars` of the line the clip was actually made from, so src/script.ts stays correct with no edit.

## Flow
- pnpm narrate after editing two lines and recasting mira
- plan: changed 1.3 (line), 2.4 (line); voice: 0.2, 3.1 (mira); reused 22; spend 611 chars
- synthesise those four, measure, write durations + manifest (sha, true chars)
- the recorder's isStale and the plan agree; no --only/--force needed

## Expected impact
A re-take is one command instead of an id hunt plus --force; a same-length edit or a recast is never silently kept; a dry rehearsal no longer corrupts measured lengths; paid characters are spent only on lines that changed, and the operator sees the bill before it is spent.

## Evaluation
Claim: content-addressed planning re-voices exactly the changed beats and never launders a stale clip
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no plan module; cases 0, 1, 3 are live defects)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases under node --test with an fs/fetch stub
Result: better
Gate: none
